item.description: - **Fixed: a failing radio was opened again and again.** A dongle that stopped answering (empty USB descriptors, register writes timing out) was re-opened every 2 to 60 s, and each open could make the driver reset it, which can stall other devices on the same USB hub. After three failures in a row the radio now reads `NOT_ANSWERING` in `ley devices`, `ley state` and the app's device menu, with what to do: "unplug it and plug it back in, ideally into a port on the back of the Mac". Leyline leaves it alone until it is replugged. A radio another program holds still reads `IN_USE` and is checked again as before. - **Fixed: a capture whose radio stopped sending samples still read `active`.** After 5 s with no samples a capture now reads `STALLED`, "no samples from <radio> for 5 s", and goes back to active when samples return. After 30 s Leyline closes and reopens the radio once; a radio that still sends nothing is marked not answering. - **Speech on a channel that never goes quiet.** A transmission longer than 30 s is cut into pieces at the quietest moment near each 30 s, with nothing lost between them, so FM broadcast, a NOAA weather station or a channel with the squelch off is transcribed rather than dropped after ten minutes. A continuous recording, which has no squelch openings, can be transcribed now: `ley transcribe` and the Library's Transcribe count every minute of it. Each piece after the first is marked `continues`. - **Fixed: speech on FM broadcast heard distorted audio.** A live speech job always made its own NFM channel. Start in the Decoders place now transcribes the channel you are listening to, in its mode and through its squelch, and `ley decode speech --channel this` does the same. With only `--freq`, the job's channel takes the band's mode, as `ley tune` does: WFM on broadcast FM, AM on airband. - **The cost of that is stated first.** A channel whose squelch never closes sends all of its audio, 60 minutes an hour. `ley decode speech` and `ley watch speech` on a channel with its squelch off, in WFM, or on FM or AM broadcast or NOAA weather say so before they start and ask; `--yes` skips the question. - **The Decoders log reads top to bottom.** The newest record is at the bottom, as `ley decode` prints it, and the log follows it. Scroll up and it stops: new records wait below without moving what you are reading, counted on a **↓ N new** button in the corner that takes you back down. Scrolling back to the bottom follows again. A log whose records name no transmitter or kind, such as speech's, no longer keeps an empty column for each: the words start beside the time, and a column appears once a record has something to put in it. - **The Decoders inspector says each thing once.** A field the record's line already shows whole, such as speech's text, is no longer listed again under Fields, and the description under each field has moved into its label's tooltip. The raw bytes are folded away under **Raw · N bytes**, which stays open once you open it; a long payload shows eight lines and **Show all**. A record whose raw bytes are only its text again, a speech transcript, has no Raw at all.

- **Fixed: the Decoders map jumped around.** It re-fitted itself to every aircraft several times a second, so it zoomed as aircraft appeared, moved and aged out. It now frames once, afterwards only zooms out when an aircraft would leave the view, and never moves when one disappears. Once you pan or zoom it stays where you put it; **Fit All** in its corner frames everything again. An aircraft not heard for half its silence window draws dimmed before it goes. - **Fixed: decoded transmitters vanished and came back.** Leaving the Decoders place, switching decoder or a reconnect rebuilt the table from only the last 1000 records, so a transmitter whose records had scrolled out disappeared until it was heard again. The table now lasts the session and new history merges into it. - **Fixed: `--for` recordings ran long or short.** On a busy Mac a `ley record --for 1s` could hold 1.1 s of audio, or stop a few milliseconds early by the clock, and a gated part could hold a few milliseconds more audio than its span. A duration is now cut at exactly its sample count, and audio is dated where its samples belong.

- **ADS-B.** A new decoder hears aircraft on 1090 MHz: `ley decode aircraft` prints each identification, position and velocity, and `ley track aircraft` keeps a table of aircraft by callsign. Its recipe sets the gain to 40 dB: on an R820T dongle over `rtl_tcp` (2026-11-02), 30 dB decoded nothing and 40 dB decoded 19 messages in 9 s. An aircraft leaves the table after 120 s with no message. - **The Decoders place (⌘3).** A third place beside Radio and Library: a sidebar of installed decoders and their running jobs, and for each a log of records, a table of transmitters, a map when records carry a position, and an inspector for the selected record. The inspector names a transmitter, and `ley label` reads the same name. A decoder started here keeps running after the app quits, until Stop. - **Starting a decoder says where it will run.** The page shows whether a decoder runs beside what you hear, takes an idle radio, or needs the radio from you; in that case Start asks "Take the radio?" naming your channel. A decoder no radio can hear has Start switched off and says why. - **Notify Me.** A decoder's page builds a watch from its fields (SAME's county, an APRS callsign, a place and radius for anything with a position) and posts a macOS notification on each match. The daemon runs the watch, so it notifies with the app closed. The sidebar lists each watch with its condition and a Stop. - **Decode With.** The Library's context menu and a recording's inspector run any installed decoder over an audio or IQ recording. The inspector's Decoded row says how many records each decoder found, with a link to its page. `ley decode <decoder> --recording <id>` does the same. - **Decoding from the Radio.** A row per running decoder tops the Radio sidebar with its count and opens its page, and the waterfall tags an APRS or other audio decoder's transmitter by name on the row it was heard in. View > Show Decoded Names turns the tags off. - **Changed: `ley tune` will not pause a decoder.** `ley tune`, `ley set freq`, `ley spectrum`, `ley waterfall` and the other verbs that retune a radio refuse a move that would pause a running job (a decoder, a watch, a recording or a scan) and list it: `retuning to 150.000 MHz would pause the aprs decoder on 144.390 MHz; --retune moves it anyway`. Before, only recordings and other clients' channels stopped a retune. - **Changed: the app asks before it moves a radio a job uses.** "Move the radio?" lists every job the move would pause, for a click or a typed frequency outside the span, a band, a narrower width or Scan band; a drag asks once. Cancel leaves the radio where it is. - **A radio comes back.** When a decoder, a scan or a take-over moved the radio and ends, the radio returns to the tuning it found, unless you moved it since. A job paused by a move says who moved it ("paused: the app tuned NESDR SMArt v5 to 146.520 MHz"), and the Radio inspector's Claims group lists who is using the radio, "paused by the app at 14:05" among them. - **Who uses a radio.** `ley state` lists each capture's users: channels, jobs, views and you. `--dry-run` on `ley decode`, `ley record` and `ley scan`, and `dry_run` on the MCP tools, say where a job would run and what it would pause, and start nothing. Several decoders share one capture, and an IQ recording starts a new part each time its radio is retuned. - **Readable records everywhere.** Each decoder's manifest carries display templates, so `ley decode`, `ley records`, `ley watch`, `ley track` and the MCP tools print one line a person reads. AIS static reports and SAME alerts, which printed raw bytes, now read as text. Fields have labels ("Transmitter", "Callsign", "County"), which `ley track`'s column heads, `ley watch`'s banner and the app use. - **Changed: `ley track` lists rows by name.** Rows were newest-heard first, so a live ADS-B table moved on every redraw; `--sort heard` keeps that order. `--json` and the MCP `list_entities` tool follow. - **`--gain` on `ley decode` and `ley watch`**, and on the MCP decode and watch tools, overrides a recipe's gain when the job sets up the radio. A job on a radio it shares keeps that radio's gain and says which. - **The decoder list** leaves out `speech-scripted` and `iqstat`, which exist for tests. - **Fixes.** `ley decode`, `ley watch` and `ley track` end with the reason when the daemon declines their job, where they waited forever. `ley watch --detach` reports a decline rather than "left running", and the MCP `watch` and `start_decode_job` tools return it. A relative `--socket` reaches the daemon. The decoder inspector's values line up in one column. Renaming a bookmark added from a scan hit on a bookmarked frequency edits that bookmark. - **Fixed: a decoder started just after another program released the dongle ran at 0 dB.** A daemon that started while `rtl_tcp` (or SDR++, GQRX) held the dongle never learned its gain table, so a decoder that opened the dongle afterwards asked for 40 dB and got 0 dB, and heard nothing. Opening the dongle now reads its tuner and gains, a fixed gain on a stage with no table is refused rather than set to 0 dB, and the `ley decode` banner names the gain. A decode job whose radio stops delivering samples for 5 s now says so (`no samples from … for 5 s`). - **Fixed: a transcription of a recording lost overs.** A recording of more than nine overs came back with most of them missing and no warning. The engine now waits for the speech decoder instead of dropping an over, and a finished job's detail says how many overs have no record (`3 of 20 overs have no record`). - **The Library lists transmissions, not files.** A row is one transmission with its transcript line under it, and a file that holds several overs (any recording made before this release, or with a long `--hang`) is a row for each, which plays that over alone. The inspector describes the transmission and its recording. When a transcription leaves some transmissions without words, the page says how many, with Transcribe again beside the count. Show in Finder moved to a row's context menu. - **Changed: a recording is one file per transmission.** A gated recording now closes a file 500 ms after the key-down in `ley record`, the MCP `record` tool and a live speech job's clips, as the app's record button already did; it was 5 s, which put an exchange of several overs in one file. `--hang 5s` (MCP `hang_ms`) keeps the old behaviour. - **Changed: `ley record` skips the dead air.** With no `--gate`, an NFM or AM recording with a squelch set is gated, so a repeater is recorded only while it is keyed; WFM, IQ and `--squelch off` still record continuously, and `--gate none` asks for that on any channel. The banner names the gate the daemon chose. The daemon also removes, at start, recordings that hold no file and were left from before an empty recording was discarded.
